title: Min Adjacent-Difference Subsequence of Length K
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers and an integer `k`.

A **subsequence** of `a` is obtained by deleting zero or more elements without changing the order of the remaining ones. The **special value** of a subsequence `p` of length `m` is the sum of absolute differences between consecutive elements:

`special(p) = |p[2] - p[1]| + |p[3] - p[2]| + ... + |p[m] - p[m-1]|`

A subsequence with a single element has special value `0`.

Among all subsequences of `a` that have **exactly `k` elements**, find the minimum special value and print it. (Because `k ≤ n`, such a subsequence always exists.)

The original problem allowed `n` up to 10^5 and `k` up to 50 with a segment tree or BIT; the limits below are scaled so that the same layered DP with a Fenwick tree runs comfortably in all languages.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[1], ..., a[n]`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum special value over all subsequences of length `k`.

examples.explanation: Choose the subsequence `1, 2, 3` (positions 1, 3, 5). Its special value is `|2-1| + |3-2| = 2`. Any 3 elements span a range of at least 2 here, and the special value is never smaller than the range, so 2 is optimal.
With k = 2 we only choose a pair in array order. The pair `8, 9` has difference 1, which is the best possible; `10, 9` also gives 1.
A subsequence of one element has no adjacent pairs, so its special value is 0.

hints: Let `dp[j][i]` be the minimum special value of a subsequence of length `j` that ends at position `i`. The transition is `dp[j][i] = min over p < i of dp[j-1][p] + |a[i] - a[p]|`. Done naively this is O(n^2 k).

Split the absolute value by comparing values: if `a[p] ≤ a[i]` the cost is `(dp[j-1][p] - a[p]) + a[i]`, otherwise it is `(dp[j-1][p] + a[p]) - a[i]`. So you need the minimum of one quantity over earlier positions with value ≤ `a[i]`, and of another over earlier positions with value ≥ `a[i]`.

Sweep positions left to right inside each layer `j`, keeping two Fenwick trees (prefix minima) indexed by the compressed value: one for `dp - a` and one for `dp + a` (on reversed ranks). Build each layer from the previous layer only.

import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
    a = [int(x) for x in data[2:2 + n]]
    if k == 1:
        print(0)
        return
    vals = sorted(set(a))
    m = len(vals)
    rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(vals)}
    r = [rank[x] for x in a]
    INF = 1 << 60
    prev = [0] * n          # prev[i]: best cost of a subsequence of the current length ending at i
    for _ in range(k - 1):
        lo = [INF] * (m + 1)   # Fenwick over value rank: min(prev[j] - a[j]), prefix min
        hi = [INF] * (m + 1)   # Fenwick over reversed rank: min(prev[j] + a[j]), prefix min
        cur = [INF] * n
        for i in range(n):
            ai, ri = a[i], r[i]
            q1 = INF
            j = ri
            while j > 0:
                if lo[j] < q1:
                    q1 = lo[j]
                j -= j & -j
            q2 = INF
            j = m + 1 - ri
            while j > 0:
                if hi[j] < q2:
                    q2 = hi[j]
                j -= j & -j
            c = INF
            if q1 < INF:
                c = q1 + ai
            if q2 < INF and q2 - ai < c:
                c = q2 - ai
            cur[i] = c
            p = prev[i]
            if p < INF:
                v = p - ai
                j = ri
                while j <= m:
                    if v < lo[j]:
                        lo[j] = v
                    j += j & -j
                v = p + ai
                j = m + 1 - ri
                while j <= m:
                    if v < hi[j]:
                        hi[j] = v
                    j += j & -j
        prev = cur
    print(min(prev))

main()

        return f'{len(a)} {k}\n' + ' '.join(map(str, a))
    tests = [fmt(1, [5]), fmt(1, [3, 9, 1]), fmt(2, [4, 4]), fmt(3, [7, 7, 7, 7]), fmt(2, [1, 1000000]),
             fmt(4, [1, 2, 3, 4]), fmt(3, [9, 1, 9, 1, 9]), fmt(5, [5, 4, 3, 2, 1])]
    for n in (3, 5, 8, 12, 20, 30):
        for _ in range(3):
            k = rng.randint(1, min(n, 8))
            hi = rng.choice([5, 30, 1000])
            tests.append(fmt(k, [rng.randint(1, hi) for _ in range(n)]))
    N, K, L = 15000, 10, 10**6
    tests.append(fmt(K, [rng.randint(1, L) for _ in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(K, sorted(rng.randint(1, L) for _ in range(N))))
    tests.append(fmt(K, [rng.choice([1, L]) if i % 2 else rng.randint(1, L) for i in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(K, [rng.randint(1, 50) for _ in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(9, [L - i for i in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(1, [rng.randint(1, L) for _ in range(N)]))
    tests.append(fmt(K, [rng.randint(1, L) for _ in range(3000)]))
    return tests
